subject.title: fix(memory-wiki): reject oversized apply body files

question: Should `wiki apply synthesis --body-file` preserve acceptance of existing larger regular files, or should OpenClaw adopt and document a new maximum input size?
rationale: The previous command accepted regular body files without this cap; selecting an arbitrary new rejection threshold is a user-visible CLI compatibility decision that source inspection cannot safely make.

options.title: Preserve existing input compatibility
options.body: Avoid an arbitrary new rejection limit, use a bounded implementation tied to an established downstream constraint if one exists, and validate the opened handle before reading.

options.title: Adopt a documented size contract
options.body: Approve a specific maximum body-file size, document the upgrade behavior and error, validate the opened handle, and add coverage for the chosen boundary.

options.title: Pause the PR
options.body: Hold this change until the memory-wiki owner defines the supported large-input behavior and its resource-safety boundary.

recommendation.title: Preserve existing input compatibility
recommendation.body: Avoid an arbitrary new rejection limit, use a bounded implementation tied to an established downstream constraint if one exists, and validate the opened handle before reading.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest available discussion-routing signal, although repository-history ownership could not be confirmed.
